item.title: The Ripple Effect of Going for It
item.description: Can you learn to captain a yacht at 62 and turn it into a world-traveling lifestyle? Absolutely! Below, Sine Maria shares a first-hand account of her family’s latest charter with Dream Yacht in the Balearic Islands. Read on for an inspiring look at courage, partnership, and what happens when you say yes to a new adventure on the water. The Ripple Effect of Going for It On breaking into worlds you weren’t born into, and what happens when you actually do the thing. By: Good Life Designed and Sine Maria If there’s one thing I’ve learned from my mom, it’s that life has so much to offer and the limit of your world is only limited by your ability to keep expanding. In the middle of the pandemic, as part of our collective pause, she and I decided to go through the whole Good Life Designed program together again. It was through that process that she decided she wanted to be closer to nature, swim more, and learn how to sail. She didn’t grow up around sailing, knew it was costly and a bit of a boys club, but always admired the access it gave those who knew how. That hobby could take you anywhere in the world. The world of sailing requires a unique blend of resources, courage, technical education, practice, and willing crew members to go along for the ride and be there while you figure things out on your first trips alone. It thrives behind heavy yacht club doors that some are born with access into – but most don’t even know exist. The dream of being certified as a sailor has an even smaller niche- attracting those who thrive on the pressure to read and respond to the chaos of the elements at sea while holding the responsibility of passengers’ lives in their hands. Now that I have experienced the reward that comes with that kind of responsibility – I see the draw. Breaking Into a World You Weren’t Born Into I tried to look into data about women certified sailors but couldn’t find any credible data because no one seems to be particularly interested in that stat – however I can tell you there aren’t many. Sailing, just due to the nature of it, the time it requires, the unease that comes with the experience, especially as you’re getting your first solo trips under your belt, is enough to send anyone right over the edge. It’s heady, it’s overwhelming, it’s complicated, it’s technical, and it feels uncertain and dangerous before you’re skilled and experienced enough to feel truly comfortable and at ease on the water. When Pernille got the ping to learn to sail, the biggest question was how, as a 62-year-old woman, was she going to do it. She tried visiting yacht clubs but as someone who wasn’t interested in the social component and was really looking for the technical skills to captain her own ship, it didn’t feel like the best place to spend her time or money. The classes and day sail opportunities to get out on the water were nice, but if she really wanted to learn everything she needed to, she needed something different. She came across Nautilus Sailing, a week-long course in the Sea of Cortez that would teach you everything you need to know about sailing and cap off the week with a test that would certify you to sail on your own anywhere in the world. My dad at the time was in the most stressful period of his career, navigating his independent school and their 400 families through Covid. Using his coveted spring break to learn to navigate another set of uncharted territories felt not quite like the vacation he needed. But he took a leap of his own and joined her anyway. They spent a week disconnected from everything to focus on learning the thing that would later give them access to the life they live now – barely imaginable to them then. Heading out on what feel like once-in-a-lifetime week long sailing experiences all over the world with friends and family. item.title: Savor the journey: Slow travel to a Med sailing paradise
item.description: As the world becomes increasingly fast-paced and disconnected, a growing number of travelers are seeking a more relaxed and immersive way to spend their precious holiday time with loved ones. This is where the concept of “slow travel” comes in – a trend that’s all about embracing the journey, not just the destination. By ditching the hustle and bustle of flights and connections, slow travelers can unwind, soak up the scenery, and make the relaxed journey a welcome part of their unique holiday experience. For travelers located in Europe, Dream Yacht’s popular charter destinations are particularly well-suited to help you jump aboard the slow travel trend. With base location in some of the Mediterranean’s most sought-after and accessible destinations such as Croatia , Mallorca and Corsica , you can easily combine your overland journey with a relaxing yacht charter vacation, exploring the crystal-clear waters and charming islands of the Mediterranean at your own pace. Not only does slow travel reduce carbon emissions and promote sustainability, but it also allows you to connect with local cultures, meet fellow travelers, and experience the authentic charm of Europe’s hidden gems. As people increasingly seek meaningful and environmentally-friendly travel experiences, it’s no wonder that slow travel has become a popular option for those seeking to reach the balmy Mediterranean in style. With our wide range of sailing itineraries and flexible charter options , Dream Yacht provides the perfect platform for slow travelers to unwind and immerse themselves in the unique culture and beauty of the Mediterranean. Ready to slow down? Why consider slower, immersive travel Slow travel often encourages travelers to adopt a more mindful and immersive approach to their journey, which can lead to a greater appreciation for local cultures and environments. By taking the time to explore destinations at a leisurely pace, travelers are more likely to engage with local communities, support small businesses, and respect the natural beauty of the places they visit. Imagine meandering through picturesque landscapes by train, watching the countryside roll by as you sip coffee or enjoy a leisurely lunch. Or, picture yourself cruising across calm waters by ferry, feeling the sea breeze on your face as you gaze out at the horizon. For those heading to popular Mediterranean yacht charter destinations, slow travel is the perfect way to set the tone for a relaxing and rejuvenating oceanic getaway. By combining train or ferry travel with a yacht charter vacation, guests can indulge in a unique and unforgettable slow travel experience that combines the best of both worlds — scenic overland journeys and tranquil seascapes. Slow travel for reduced emissions Your slow travel journey can also help to reduce waste and promote sustainable tourism practices, such as choosing eco-friendly accommodations and activities. In particular, traveling by train and ferry can significantly help reduce carbon footprint compared to flying. Trains and ferries generally produce fewer greenhouse gas emissions per passenger than planes. According to the European Environment Agency, trains produce around 14 grams of CO2 per passenger-kilometer, while ferries produce around 21 grams of CO2 per passenger-kilometer. In contrast, planes produce around 285 grams of CO2 per passenger-kilometer. Trains and ferries are shared modes of transportation, which means that the emissions are spread out among a larger number of passengers. This makes them a more environmentally friendly option than driving. Perhaps try one of these CO2 calculators to see how much more efficient your journey could be! www.ecopassenger.org/ www.greentripper.org/ Slow travel routes to Dream Yacht bases from France & the UK Several Dream Yacht locations are quite accessible from France and the UK, offering a tantalizing escape to a sun-kissed Mediterranean paradise with just a few hours of travel. item.title: Are you qualified for a bareboat yacht charter?
item.description: If you want to go on a sailing vacation but are unsure if your sailing experience means you are qualified for a bareboat yacht charter, we’ve got some tips and advice for you. Your safety is important to us and it’s important that you are able to handle your yacht in your chosen destination. For bareboat yacht charters, we expect you to have experience sailing a boat of similar size. It’s also helpful to have at least one crew member of similar experience. For most destinations, you do not need bareboat charter certification. Learn more about our bareboat yacht charters . Getting ready for sailing We usually ask that you have sailing experience on a boat of similar size. It’s also helpful to have at least one crew member of similar experience. While a bareboat charter certificate is not usually mandatory, safety is always our #1 priority. Even if you’re highly experienced, we recommend that you take sailing courses from reputable organizations. Refresh your knowledge on anchoring, navigation, maneuvering a large sailboat in a tight marina, and other nuances of bareboat chartering. If you are still unsure of your sailing abilities, or simply want the knowledge of a local skipper, you can hire a professional captain at a daily rate, then continue on your own when you feel comfortable. If you’d rather not cook, hire a chef and have all of your meals prepared for you. Contact us for more information. Finding the right destination for your sailing experience You will find information on the local cruising ground, wind systems and weather conditions on our destination pages . Our expert team can help you if you want to know the level of experience required for your chosen destination and if you are qualified for a bareboat yacht charter. Contact our team . We can advise where to find line of sight navigation and calm waters. Also, we can help if you are looking for a challenge. The British Virgin Islands are popular because of the calm waters and easy navigation. If you’re after a relaxing sailing vacation, try Corfu and Lefkas in Greece as the Ionian Islands offer plenty of short leg island hopping. Our bases in the Exumas and Australia’s Whitsunday Islands are good for sailors who don’t want an energetic sail. Sailors seeking more of a challenge can look for bareboat yacht charters from our Cyclades Islands bases in Paros and Mykonos in Greece, with its Meltemi wind system. Croatia , with its Bora wind, can also offer some fast sailing conditions at the right time of year. When do you need an accredited sailing license? Bareboat certification is not usually mandatory in most destinations, but you need to check the specific license requirements of your chosen destination to know if you are qualified for a bareboat yacht charter. What about Europe? Some destinations, particularly in the Mediterranean, require official sailing certification or licensure from a recognized organization, such as an International Certificate of Competence (ICC) or equivalent qualification. Our destination base guides indicate if you need a recognized sailing license. In these cases, the local authorities may require the skipper to prove their bareboat sailing proficiency. The skipper will need to take original copies of their bareboat certification with them on charter. Before you book your charter vacation, ensure that you have the required sailing certification that is accepted by the country you are sailing in. Unsure about your destination’s requirements? Contact our team . What if I don’t have proof of competence? If you don’t have the right bareboat certification for your chosen destination, you can always add a skipper , which offers many benefits. Skippers have excellent local knowledge and the best recommendations for local anchorages and restaurants to make the most of your vacation.
